## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests
- Test controller logic in isolation
- Mock external dependencies (database, email service)
- Verify input validation and error handling

### Integration Tests
- Test full request-response cycle
- Use test containers or in-memory database
- Verify database operations and constraints

### Test Cases
- Valid user creation (201 status)
- Invalid email format (400 status)
- Duplicate email (409 status)
- Database connection error (500 status)
- Missing required fields (400 status)

### Tools
- Jest/Mocha for test framework
- Supertest for HTTP assertions
- Testcontainers for database integration

## Why This Is Asked
Tests for event-driven architectures where ordering, deduplication, and replay safety matter for correctness and fault tolerance in production.

## Key Concepts
- Event-driven pipelines, at-least-once vs exactly-once
- Idempotent consumers and deduplication
- Replay safety and late-arriving events
- End-to-end and read-model validation
- Observability and metrics

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-idempotent consumer sketch
async function handleEvent(evt){
  const {id, type, payload} = evt
  if(await redis.exists(id)) return // dedupe
  await redis.set(id, true, 'EX', 3600)
  switch(type){
    case 'order.created': await processOrder(payload); break
    // …
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure dedupe effectiveness and latency impact?
- How would schema evolution be handled in tests (AVRO/Protobuf)?
